quizzes.title: Strategic Significance of INS Aridaman: MCQ
quizzes.passage: India commissioned INS Aridaman, its third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, and the booklet notes that this milestone brings the number of operational SSBNs at sea to three. Ships of this class are described as carrying ballistic missiles that may be nuclear armed. In the same news item, the stealth frigate INS Taragiri, the fourth ship of Project 17A, was commissioned at Visakhapatnam. The booklet's section on the submarine's importance sets out a number of effects under separate headings. These concern the ways in which nuclear weapons can be delivered, the country's standing among states, the reach of its navy, and the policy framework that guides its use of nuclear weapons. The booklet frames these points under the heading of strategic significance. The booklet compares the three Arihant-class boats, INS Arihant, INS Arighaat and INS Aridaman, and notes that their specifications are classified. Its sketch is only an approximation, credited to Wikimedia Commons. Each boat in that comparison is listed by its commissioning year, displacement and the missiles it is believed to carry. Taken together, these entries give the booklet's overview of the class. The booklet's list of strategic effects gives each point a single line. These pages run from page 56 to page 57 of the booklet.

questions.q: Which doctrine is the submarine's second-strike capability said to support?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the second-strike capability supports India's No First Use doctrine.

questions.q: According to the booklet, the submarine improves India's strategic reach in which regions?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the submarine improves strategic reach in the Indian Ocean Region and Indo-Pacific.

questions.q: Which country is NOT listed by the booklet among the countries with operational nuclear triads?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists USA, Russia, UK, China and France, so Germany is the one not listed.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India can deliver nuclear weapons from land, air and sea.
Reason (R): INS Aridaman completes India's nuclear triad.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says completing the nuclear triad enables nuclear delivery via land, air and sea, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Second Strike Capability   ->   A. Enables nuclear delivery via land, air and sea
II. Completion of Nuclear Triad   ->   B. Provides assured retaliation capability
III. Enhanced Deterrence   ->   C. Places India among countries with operational nuclear triads
IV. Global Strategic Status   ->   D. Improves strategic reach in Indian Ocean Region and Indo-Pacific
questions.explanation: The booklet pairs second strike with assured retaliation, the triad with land, air and sea delivery, enhanced deterrence with strategic reach, and global status with the list of nuclear-triad countries.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The submarine boosts Credible Minimum Deterrence.
II. The booklet lists the UK among countries with operational nuclear triads.
III. The booklet lists Japan among countries with operational nuclear triads.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while Japan is not in the booklet's list, so only I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Of the statements below, how many are correct?
I. The submarine is said to improve strategic reach in the Arctic region.
II. The submarine boosts Credible Minimum Deterrence.
III. The submarine supports the No First Use doctrine.
questions.explanation: Statements II and III are in the booklet, while statement I names the Arctic instead of the Indian Ocean Region and Indo-Pacific.

questions.q: Along with the Indo-Pacific, which ocean region does the booklet say the submarine improves strategic reach in?

questions.q: What is the expansion of CMD in the booklet's strategic significance section?

quizzes.title: Submarine Building Programmes: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The booklet presents India's submarine programme as a long-term effort. After the Kargil War, the Cabinet Committee on Security approved a 30-year Submarine Building Plan with the aim of building conventional submarines indigenously. The booklet describes Project 75 as Phase I of the Indian Navy's 30-year indigenous submarine construction plan. Under this project, diesel-electric attack submarines of the Kalvari class were being built at Mazagon Dock Limited, and the booklet records the commissioning of one of them. Two production lines were planned, using transfer of technology from different foreign manufacturers. The booklet also notes that private Indian firms take part alongside foreign manufacturers under the Make in India initiative in defence. The booklet also lists Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited, together with Larsen & Toubro Limited, as shortlisted to partner with foreign submarine manufacturers. Mazagon Dock appears in this section both as a builder and as a shortlisted partner. The booklet says conventional diesel-electric submarines of this type come with improved stealth features. The Project 75 entry is followed by a separate entry for the later project. The topic appears in the booklet's April 2026 current affairs section. The booklet's submarine section sits alongside a note on the Indian Navy's ships and its history. Its page on the navy also gives a short history of the force.

questions.q: In which year was Project 75I approved as Phase II of the Indian Navy's 30-year plan?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Project 75I was approved in 2007 as Phase II.

questions.q: Project 75I is the first project under which model?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Project 75I as the first project under the Strategic Partnership Model.

questions.q: For how long can submarines built under the AIP-based project stay submerged?
questions.explanation: The booklet says AIP technology lets submarines in that project stay submerged for up to 2 weeks.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Project 75I is the first project under the Strategic Partnership Model.
Reason (R): Project 75 is Phase I of the Indian Navy's 30-year indigenous submarine plan.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the Phase I description of Project 75 does not explain why Project 75I is under the partnership model.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering   ->   A. Russia
II. Naval Group   ->   B. France
III. Rosoboronexport   ->   C. South Korea
IV. Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS)   ->   D. Germany
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Daewoo as South Korean, Naval Group as French, Rosoboronexport as Russian and TKMS as German.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Project 75I was approved in 2007 as Phase II.
II. The AIP-based project lets submarines stay submerged for up to 1 month.
III. Five foreign OEMs were named, including Naval Group of France.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I and III match the booklet, while the booklet gives up to 2 weeks, not 1 month, for submerged operation.

questions.q:
Of the statements below, how many are correct?
I. Project 75 is Phase I of the Indian Navy's 30-year plan.
II. Conventional diesel-electric submarines need to surface every 24 hours to recharge.
III. Project 75I aims to procure submarines with fuel cells and AIP.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while the booklet gives 48 hours, not 24, for conventional submarines to surface.
